description:
The terminal emulator program to use when using Open in Terminal context menu action in the FileSystem dock. You can enter an absolute path to a program binary, or a path to a program that is present in the PATH environment variable.

If left empty, Godot will use the default terminal emulator for the system:

- Windows: PowerShell

- macOS: Terminal.app

- Linux: The first terminal found on the system in this order: gnome-terminal, konsole, xfce4-terminal, lxterminal, kitty, alacritty, urxvt, xterm.

To use Command Prompt (cmd) instead of PowerShell on Windows, enter cmd in this field and the correct flags will automatically be used.

On macOS, make sure to point to the actual program binary located within the Programs/MacOS folder of the .app bundle, rather than the .app bundle directory.

If specifying a custom terminal emulator, you may need to override filesystem/external_programs/terminal_emulator_flags so it opens in the correct folder.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/external_programs/terminal_emulator
name: filesystem/external_programs/terminal_emulator

description:
The command-line arguments to pass to the terminal emulator that is run when using Open in Terminal context menu action in the FileSystem dock. See also filesystem/external_programs/terminal_emulator.

If left empty, the default flags are {directory}, which is replaced by the absolute path to the directory that is being opened in the terminal.

\ Note: If the terminal emulator is set to PowerShell, cmd, or Konsole, Godot will automatically prepend arguments to this list, as these terminals require nonstandard arguments to open in the correct folder.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/external_programs/terminal_emulator_flags
name: filesystem/external_programs/terminal_emulator_flags

description: The program that opens vector image files when clicking "Open in External Program" option in Filesystem Dock. If not specified, the file will be opened in the system's default program.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/external_programs/vector_image_editor
name: filesystem/external_programs/vector_image_editor

description:
The display mode to use in the editor's file dialogs.

- Thumbnails takes more space, but displays dynamic resource thumbnails, making resources easier to preview without having to open them.

- List is more compact but doesn't display dynamic resource thumbnails. Instead, it displays static icons based on the file extension.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/file_dialog/display_mode
name: filesystem/file_dialog/display_mode

description: If true, display hidden files in the editor's file dialogs. Files that have names starting with . are considered hidden (e.g. .hidden_file).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/file_dialog/show_hidden_files
name: filesystem/file_dialog/show_hidden_files

description: The thumbnail size to use in the editor's file dialogs (in pixels). See also docks/filesystem/thumbnail_size.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/file_dialog/thumbnail_size
name: filesystem/file_dialog/thumbnail_size

description: Password used for file server when exporting project with remote file system.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/file_server/password
name: filesystem/file_server/password

description: Port used for file server when exporting project with remote file system.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/file_server/port
name: filesystem/file_server/port

description:
The path to the Blender executable used for converting the Blender 3D scene files .blend to glTF 2.0 format during import. Blender 3.0 or later is required.

To enable this feature for your specific project, use ProjectSettings.filesystem/import/blender/enabled.

If this setting is empty, Blender's default paths will be detected and used automatically if present in this order:

\ Windows:\

- C:Program FilesBlender Foundationblender.exe
- C:Program Files (x86)Blender Foundationblender.exe

\ macOS:\

- /opt/homebrew/bin/blender
- /opt/local/bin/blender
- /usr/local/bin/blender
- /usr/local/opt/blender
- /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender

\ Linux/BSD:\

- /usr/bin/blender
- /usr/local/bin/blender
- /opt/blender/bin/blender
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/import/blender/blender_path
name: filesystem/import/blender/blender_path

description:
The port number used for Remote Procedure Call (RPC) communication with Godot's created process of the blender executable.

Setting this to 0 effectively disables communication with Godot and the blender process, making performance slower.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/import/blender/rpc_port
name: filesystem/import/blender/rpc_port

description:
The maximum idle uptime (in seconds) of the Blender process.

This prevents Godot from having to create a new process for each import within the given seconds.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/import/blender/rpc_server_uptime
name: filesystem/import/blender/rpc_server_uptime

description:
The path to the FBX2glTF executable used for converting Autodesk FBX 3D scene files .fbx to glTF 2.0 format during import.

To enable this feature for your specific project, use ProjectSettings.filesystem/import/fbx2gltf/enabled.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/import/fbx/fbx2gltf_path
name: filesystem/import/fbx/fbx2gltf_path

description: If true, uses lossless compression for binary resources.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/on_save/compress_binary_resources
name: filesystem/on_save/compress_binary_resources

description:
If true, when saving a file, the editor will rename the old file to a different name, save a new file, then only remove the old file once the new file has been saved. This makes loss of data less likely to happen if the editor or operating system exits unexpectedly while saving (e.g. due to a crash or power outage).

\ Note: On Windows, this feature can interact negatively with certain antivirus programs. In this case, you may have to set this to false to prevent file locking issues.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/on_save/safe_save_on_backup_then_rename
name: filesystem/on_save/safe_save_on_backup_then_rename

description:
If true, displays a warning toast message when saving a text-based scene or resource that is larger than 500 KiB on disk. This is typically caused by binary subresources being embedded as text, which results in slow and inefficient conversion to text. This in turn impacts scene saving and loading times.

This should usually be resolved by moving the embedded binary subresource to its own binary resource file (.res extension instead of .tres). This is the preferred approach. Alternatively, the entire scene can be saved with the binary .scn format as opposed to .tscn, but this will make it less friendly to version control systems.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/on_save/warn_on_saving_large_text_resources
name: filesystem/on_save/warn_on_saving_large_text_resources

description: If set to Adaptive, the dialog opens in list view or grid view depending on the requested type. If set to Last Used, the display mode will always open the way you last used it.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/quick_open_dialog/default_display_mode
name: filesystem/quick_open_dialog/default_display_mode

description:
If true, together with exact matches of a filename, the dialog includes approximate matches.

This is useful for finding the correct files even when there are typos in the search query; for example, searching "nprmal" will find "normal". Additionally, it allows you to write shorter search queries; for example, searching "nml" will also find "normal".

See also filesystem/quick_open_dialog/max_fuzzy_misses.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/quick_open_dialog/enable_fuzzy_matching
name: filesystem/quick_open_dialog/enable_fuzzy_matching

description: If true, results will include files located in the addons folder.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/quick_open_dialog/include_addons
name: filesystem/quick_open_dialog/include_addons

description: If true, highlighting a resource will preview it quickly without confirming the selection or closing the dialog.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/quick_open_dialog/instant_preview
name: filesystem/quick_open_dialog/instant_preview

description: The number of missed query characters allowed in a match when fuzzy matching is enabled. For example, with the default value of 2, "normal" would match "narmal" and "norma" but not "nor".
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/quick_open_dialog/max_fuzzy_misses
name: filesystem/quick_open_dialog/max_fuzzy_misses

description: Maximum number of matches to show in dialog.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/quick_open_dialog/max_results
name: filesystem/quick_open_dialog/max_results

description: If true, results will be highlighted with their search matches.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/quick_open_dialog/show_search_highlight
name: filesystem/quick_open_dialog/show_search_highlight

description:
The path to the directory containing the Open Image Denoise (OIDN) executable, used optionally for denoising lightmaps. It can be downloaded from openimagedenoise.org <https://www.openimagedenoise.org/downloads.html>_.

To enable this feature for your specific project, use ProjectSettings.rendering/lightmapping/denoising/denoiser.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_filesystem/tools/oidn/oidn_denoise_path
name: filesystem/tools/oidn/oidn_denoise_path

description:
If true, input events will be flushed just before every idle and physics frame.

If false, these events will be flushed only once per process frame, between iterations of the engine.

Enabling this setting can greatly improve input responsiveness, especially in devices that struggle to run at the project's intended frame rate.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_input/buffering/agile_event_flushing
name: input/buffering/agile_event_flushing

description:
If true, similar input events sent by the operating system are accumulated. When input accumulation is enabled, all input events generated during a frame will be merged and emitted when the frame is done rendering. Therefore, this limits the number of input method calls per second to the rendering FPS.

Input accumulation can be disabled to get slightly more precise/reactive input at the cost of increased CPU usage.

\ Note: Input accumulation is enabled by default.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_input/buffering/use_accumulated_input
name: input/buffering/use_accumulated_input

description:
Editor accessibility support mode:

- Auto (0): Accessibility support is enabled, but updates to the accessibility information are processed only if an assistive app (such as a screen reader or a Braille display) is active (default).

- Always Active (1): Accessibility support is enabled, and updates to the accessibility information are always processed, regardless of the status of assistive apps.

- Disabled (2): Accessibility support is fully disabled.

\ Note: Accessibility debugging tools, such as Accessibility Insights for Windows, Accessibility Inspector (macOS), or AT-SPI Browser (Linux/BSD), do not count as assistive apps. To test the editor with these tools, use Always Active.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/accessibility/accessibility_support
name: interface/accessibility/accessibility_support

description: If true, editor inspector uses property documentation as an accessible description of the property.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/accessibility/property_descriptions
name: interface/accessibility/property_descriptions

description:
How to position the Cancel and OK buttons in the editor's AcceptDialog windows. Different platforms have different conventions for this, which can be overridden through this setting to avoid accidental clicks when using Godot on multiple platforms.

- Auto follows the platform convention: OK first on Windows, KDE, and LXQt; Cancel first on macOS and other Linux desktop environments.

- Cancel First forces the Cancel/OK ordering.

- OK First forces the OK/Cancel ordering.

To check if these buttons are swapped at runtime, use DisplayServer.get_swap_cancel_ok().
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/accept_dialog_cancel_ok_buttons
name: interface/editor/appearance/accept_dialog_cancel_ok_buttons

description:
If true, the main menu collapses into a MenuButton.

\ Note: This setting is only applicable on macOS when interface/editor/appearance/use_embedded_menu is true.

\ Note: Defaults to true on the Android editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/collapse_main_menu
name: interface/editor/appearance/collapse_main_menu

description:
The custom editor scale factor to use. This can be used for displays with very high DPI where a scale factor of 200% is not sufficient.

\ Note: Only effective if interface/editor/appearance/display_scale is set to Custom.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/custom_display_scale
name: interface/editor/appearance/custom_display_scale

description:
The display scale factor to use for the editor interface. Higher values are more suited to hiDPI/Retina displays.

If set to Auto, the editor scale is automatically determined based on the screen resolution and reported display DPI. This heuristic is not always ideal, which means you can get better results by setting the editor scale manually.

If set to Custom, the scaling value in interface/editor/appearance/custom_display_scale will be used.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/display_scale
name: interface/editor/appearance/display_scale

description: The preferred monitor to display the editor. If Auto, the editor will remember the last screen it was displayed on across multiple sessions.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/editor_screen
name: interface/editor/appearance/editor_screen

description:
Expanding main editor window content to the title, if supported by DisplayServer. See DisplayServer.WINDOW_FLAG_EXTEND_TO_TITLE.

Specific to the macOS platform.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/expand_to_title
name: interface/editor/appearance/expand_to_title

description: The preferred monitor to display the project manager.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/project_manager_screen
name: interface/editor/appearance/project_manager_screen

description: If true, a renderer selector that can be used to change the ProjectSettings.rendering/renderer/rendering_method project setting will be shown in the top right of the main editor window.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/show_renderer_selector
name: interface/editor/appearance/show_renderer_selector

description:
If enabled, displays an icon in the top-right corner of the editor that spins when the editor redraws a frame. This can be used to diagnose situations where the engine is constantly redrawing, which should be avoided as this increases CPU and GPU utilization for no good reason. To further troubleshoot these situations, start the editor with the --debug-canvas-item-redraw command line argument.

Consider enabling this if you are developing editor plugins to ensure they only make the editor redraw when required.

The default Auto value will only enable this if the editor was compiled with the dev_build=yes SCons option (the default is dev_build=no).

\ Note: If interface/editor/display/update_continuously is true, the spinner icon displays in red.

\ Note: If the editor was started with the --debug-canvas-item-redraw command line argument, the update spinner will never display regardless of this setting's value. This is to avoid confusion with what would cause redrawing in real world scenarios.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/show_update_spinner
name: interface/editor/appearance/show_update_spinner

description:
If true, editor main menu is using embedded MenuBar instead of system global menu.

Specific to the macOS platform.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/use_embedded_menu
name: interface/editor/appearance/use_embedded_menu

description: If true, editor UI uses OS native file/directory selection dialogs.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/appearance/use_native_file_dialogs
name: interface/editor/appearance/use_native_file_dialogs

description: If true, automatically opens screenshots with the default program associated to .png files after a screenshot is taken using the Editor > Take Screenshot action.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/behavior/automatically_open_screenshots
name: interface/editor/behavior/automatically_open_screenshots

description: If true, (re)imports resources even if the editor window is unfocused or minimized. If false, resources are only (re)imported when the editor window is focused. This can be set to true to speed up iteration by starting the import process earlier when saving files in the project folder. This also allows getting visual feedback on changes without having to click the editor window, which is useful with multi-monitor setups. The downside of setting this to true is that it increases idle CPU usage and may steal CPU time from other applications when importing resources.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/behavior/import_resources_when_unfocused
name: interface/editor/behavior/import_resources_when_unfocused

description: If false, the editor will save all scenes when confirming the Save action when quitting the editor or quitting to the project list. If true, the editor will ask to save each scene individually.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/behavior/save_each_scene_on_quit
name: interface/editor/behavior/save_each_scene_on_quit

description: If true, scenes and scripts are saved when the editor loses focus. Depending on the work flow, this behavior can be less intrusive than text_editor/behavior/files/autosave_interval_secs or remembering to save manually.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/behavior/save_on_focus_loss
name: interface/editor/behavior/save_on_focus_loss

description: If true, the editor's Script tab will have a separate distraction mode setting from the 2D/3D/Game/AssetLib tabs. If false, the distraction-free mode toggle is shared between all tabs.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/behavior/separate_distraction_mode
name: interface/editor/behavior/separate_distraction_mode

description:
If enabled, displays internal engine errors in toast notifications (toggleable by clicking the "bell" icon at the bottom of the editor). No matter the value of this setting, non-internal engine errors will always be visible in toast notifications.

The default Auto value will only enable this if the editor was compiled with the dev_build=yes SCons option (the default is dev_build=no).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/behavior/show_internal_errors_in_toast_notifications
name: interface/editor/behavior/show_internal_errors_in_toast_notifications

description: If true, keeps the screen on (even in case of inactivity), so the screensaver does not take over. Works on desktop and mobile platforms.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/display/keep_screen_on
name: interface/editor/display/keep_screen_on

description:
If true, embed modal windows such as docks inside the main editor window. When single-window mode is enabled, tooltips will also be embedded inside the main editor window, which means they can't be displayed outside of the editor window. Single-window mode can be faster as it does not need to create a separate window for every popup and tooltip, which can be a slow operation depending on the operating system and rendering method in use.

This is equivalent to ProjectSettings.display/window/subwindows/embed_subwindows in the running project, except the setting's value is inverted.

\ Note: To query whether the editor can use multiple windows in an editor plugin, use EditorInterface.is_multi_window_enabled() instead of querying the value of this editor setting.

\ Note: If true, game embedding is disabled.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/display/single_window_mode
name: interface/editor/display/single_window_mode

description:
If true, redraws the editor every frame even if nothing has changed on screen. When this setting is enabled, the update spinner displays in red (see interface/editor/appearance/show_update_spinner).

\ Warning: This greatly increases CPU and GPU utilization, leading to increased power usage. This should only be enabled for troubleshooting purposes.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/display/update_continuously
name: interface/editor/display/update_continuously

description:
Sets the V-Sync mode for the editor. Does not affect the project when run from the editor (this is controlled by ProjectSettings.display/window/vsync/vsync_mode).

Depending on the platform and used renderer, the engine will fall back to Enabled if the desired mode is not supported.

\ Note: V-Sync modes other than Enabled are only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/display/vsync_mode
name: interface/editor/display/vsync_mode

description: Tab style of editor docks located at the bottom.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/docks/bottom_dock_tab_style
name: interface/editor/docks/bottom_dock_tab_style

description: Tab style of editor docks, except bottom docks.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/docks/dock_tab_style
name: interface/editor/docks/dock_tab_style

description: The font to use for the script editor. Must be a resource of a Font type such as a .ttf or .otf font file.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/code_font
name: interface/editor/fonts/code_font

description:
The font ligatures to enable for the currently configured code font. Not all fonts include support for ligatures.

\ Note: The default editor code font (JetBrains Mono <https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/>_) has contextual ligatures in its font file.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/code_font_contextual_ligatures
name: interface/editor/fonts/code_font_contextual_ligatures

description:
List of custom OpenType features to use, if supported by the currently configured code font. Not all fonts include support for custom OpenType features. The string should follow the OpenType specification.

\ Note: The default editor code font (JetBrains Mono <https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/>_) has custom OpenType features in its font file, but there is no documented list yet.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/code_font_custom_opentype_features
name: interface/editor/fonts/code_font_custom_opentype_features

description:
List of alternative characters to use, if supported by the currently configured code font. Not all fonts include support for custom variations. The string should follow the OpenType specification.

\ Note: The default editor code font (JetBrains Mono <https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/>_) has alternate characters in its font file, but there is no documented list yet.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/code_font_custom_variations
name: interface/editor/fonts/code_font_custom_variations

description: The size of the font in the script editor. This setting does not impact the font size of the Output panel (see run/output/font_size).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/code_font_size
name: interface/editor/fonts/code_font_size

description: If set to true, MSDF font rendering will be used for the visual shader graph editor. You may need to set this to false when using a custom main font, as some fonts will look broken due to the use of self-intersecting outlines in their font data. Downloading the font from the font maker's official website as opposed to a service like Google Fonts can help resolve this issue.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/font_allow_msdf
name: interface/editor/fonts/font_allow_msdf

description: FreeType's font anti-aliasing mode used to render the editor fonts. Most fonts are not designed to look good with anti-aliasing disabled, so it's recommended to leave this enabled unless you're using a pixel art font.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/font_antialiasing
name: interface/editor/fonts/font_antialiasing

description: If set to true, embedded font bitmap loading is disabled (bitmap-only and color fonts ignore this property).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/font_disable_embedded_bitmaps
name: interface/editor/fonts/font_disable_embedded_bitmaps

description:
The font hinting mode to use for the editor fonts. FreeType supports the following font hinting modes:

- None: Don't use font hinting when rasterizing the font. This results in a smooth font, but it can look blurry.

- Light: Use hinting on the X axis only. This is a compromise between font sharpness and smoothness.

- Normal: Use hinting on both X and Y axes. This results in a sharp font, but it doesn't look very smooth.

If set to Auto, the font hinting mode will be set to match the current operating system in use. This means the Light hinting mode will be used on Windows and Linux, and the None hinting mode will be used on macOS.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/font_hinting
name: interface/editor/fonts/font_hinting

description: The subpixel positioning mode to use when rendering editor font glyphs. This affects both the main and code fonts. Disabled is the fastest to render and uses the least memory. Auto only uses subpixel positioning for small font sizes (where the benefit is the most noticeable). One Half of a Pixel and One Quarter of a Pixel force the same subpixel positioning mode for all editor fonts, regardless of their size (with One Quarter of a Pixel being the highest-quality option).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/font_subpixel_positioning
name: interface/editor/fonts/font_subpixel_positioning

description:
The font to use for the editor interface. Must be a resource of a Font type such as a .ttf or .otf font file.

\ Note: If the provided font is variable, a weight of 400 (normal) will be used.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/main_font
name: interface/editor/fonts/main_font

description:
The font to use for bold text in the editor interface. Must be a resource of a Font type such as a .ttf or .otf font file.

\ Note: If the provided font is variable, a weight of 700 (bold) will be used.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/main_font_bold
name: interface/editor/fonts/main_font_bold

description:
List of custom OpenType features to use, if supported by the currently configured main font. Check what OpenType features are supported by your font first.

The string should follow the OpenType specification, e.g. ss01,tnum,calt=false. Microsoft's documentation contains a list of all registered features <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/featurelist>_.

\ Note: The default editor main font (Inter <https://rsms.me/inter>_) has custom OpenType features in its font file, with ss04 and tnum enabled and calt disabled by default. Supported features can be found at its website.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/main_font_custom_opentype_features
name: interface/editor/fonts/main_font_custom_opentype_features

description: The size of the font in the editor interface.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/fonts/main_font_size
name: interface/editor/fonts/main_font_size

description: If true, the mouse's additional side buttons will be usable to navigate in the script editor's file history. Set this to false if you're using the side buttons for other purposes (such as a push-to-talk button in a VoIP program).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/input/mouse_extra_buttons_navigate_history
name: interface/editor/input/mouse_extra_buttons_navigate_history

description: Overrides the tablet driver used by the editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/input/tablet_driver
name: interface/editor/input/tablet_driver

description:
The language to use for the editor interface. If set to Auto, the language is automatically determined based on the system locale. See also EditorInterface.get_editor_language().

Translations are provided by the community. If you spot a mistake, contribute to editor translations on Weblate! <https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/translation/index.html>_
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/localization/editor_language
name: interface/editor/localization/editor_language

description:
If true, setting names in the editor are localized when possible.

\ Note: This setting affects most EditorInspector\ s in the editor UI, primarily Project Settings and Editor Settings. To control names displayed in the Inspector dock, use interface/inspector/default_property_name_style instead.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/localization/localize_settings
name: interface/editor/localization/localize_settings

description: Editor UI default layout direction.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/localization/ui_layout_direction
name: interface/editor/localization/ui_layout_direction

description: During a drag-and-drop, this is how long to wait over a UI element before it triggers a reaction (e.g. a section unfolds to show nested items).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/timers/dragging_hover_wait_seconds
name: interface/editor/timers/dragging_hover_wait_seconds

description:
The amount of sleeping between frames in the editor (in microseconds). Higher values will result in lower CPU/GPU usage, which can improve battery life on laptops. However, higher values will result in a less responsive editor. The default value is set to allow for maximum smoothness on monitors up to 144 Hz. See also interface/editor/timers/unfocused_low_processor_mode_sleep_usec.

\ Note: This setting is ignored if interface/editor/display/update_continuously is true, as enabling that setting disables low-processor mode.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/timers/low_processor_mode_sleep_usec
name: interface/editor/timers/low_processor_mode_sleep_usec

description:
When the editor window is unfocused, the amount of sleeping between frames when the low-processor usage mode is enabled (in microseconds). Higher values will result in lower CPU/GPU usage, which can improve battery life on laptops (in addition to improving the running project's performance if the editor has to redraw continuously). However, higher values will result in a less responsive editor. The default value is set to limit the editor to 10 FPS when the editor window is unfocused. See also interface/editor/timers/low_processor_mode_sleep_usec.

\ Note: This setting is ignored if interface/editor/display/update_continuously is true, as enabling that setting disables low-processor mode.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editor/timers/unfocused_low_processor_mode_sleep_usec
name: interface/editor/timers/unfocused_low_processor_mode_sleep_usec

description: If true, when extending a script, the global class name of the script is inserted in the script creation dialog, if it exists. If false, the script's file path is always inserted.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/editors/derive_script_globals_by_name
name: interface/editors/derive_script_globals_by_name

description:
If true, automatically unfolds Inspector property groups containing modified values when opening a scene for the first time. Only affects scenes without saved folding preferences and only unfolds groups with properties that have been changed from their default values.

\ Note: This setting only works in specific scenarios: when opening a scene brought in from another project, or when opening a new scene that already has modified properties (e.g., from version control). Duplicated scenes are not considered foreign, so this setting will not affect them.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/auto_unfold_foreign_scenes
name: interface/inspector/auto_unfold_foreign_scenes

description: If true, show the intensity slider in the ColorPicker\ s opened in the editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/color_picker_show_intensity
name: interface/inspector/color_picker_show_intensity

description: The default color picker mode to use when opening ColorPicker\ s in the editor. This mode can be temporarily adjusted on the color picker itself.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/default_color_picker_mode
name: interface/inspector/default_color_picker_mode

description: The default color picker shape to use when opening ColorPicker\ s in the editor. This shape can be temporarily adjusted on the color picker itself.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/default_color_picker_shape
name: interface/inspector/default_color_picker_shape

description: The floating-point precision to use for properties that don't define an explicit precision step. Lower values allow entering more precise values.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/default_float_step
name: interface/inspector/default_float_step

description:
The default property name style to display in the Inspector dock. This style can be temporarily adjusted in the Inspector dock's menu.

- Raw: Displays properties in snake_case.

- Capitalized: Displays properties capitalized.

- Localized: Displays the localized string for the current editor language if a translation is available for the given property. If no translation is available, falls back to Capitalized.

\ Note: To display translated setting names in Project Settings and Editor Settings, use interface/editor/localization/localize_settings instead.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/default_property_name_style
name: interface/inspector/default_property_name_style

description:
If true, add a margin around Array, Dictionary, and Resource Editors that are not already colored.

\ Note: If interface/inspector/nested_color_mode is set to Containers & Resources this parameter will have no effect since those editors will already be colored.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/delimitate_all_container_and_resources
name: interface/inspector/delimitate_all_container_and_resources

description: If true, forces all property groups to be expanded in the Inspector dock and prevents collapsing them.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/disable_folding
name: interface/inspector/disable_folding

description: Base speed for increasing/decreasing float values by dragging them in the inspector.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/float_drag_speed
name: interface/inspector/float_drag_speed

description: If true, Vector2 and Vector2i properties are shown on a single line in the inspector instead of two lines. This is overall more compact, but it can be harder to view and edit large values without expanding the inspector horizontally.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/horizontal_vector2_editing
name: interface/inspector/horizontal_vector2_editing

description: If true, Vector3, Vector3i, Vector4, Vector4i, Rect2, Rect2i, Plane, and Quaternion properties are shown on a single line in the inspector instead of multiple lines. This is overall more compact, but it can be harder to view and edit large values without expanding the inspector horizontally.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/horizontal_vector_types_editing
name: interface/inspector/horizontal_vector_types_editing

description: Base speed for increasing/decreasing integer values by dragging them in the inspector.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/integer_drag_speed
name: interface/inspector/integer_drag_speed

description: The number of Array or Dictionary items to display on each "page" in the inspector. Higher values allow viewing more values per page, but take more time to load. This increased load time is noticeable when selecting nodes that have array or dictionary properties in the editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/max_array_dictionary_items_per_page
name: interface/inspector/max_array_dictionary_items_per_page

description:
Control which property editors are colored when they are opened.

- Containers & Resources: Color all Array, Dictionary, and Resource Editors.

- Resources: Color all Resource Editors.

- External Resources: Color Resource Editors that edits an external resource.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/nested_color_mode
name: interface/inspector/nested_color_mode

description: If true, subresources can be edited in the current inspector view. If the resource type is defined in interface/inspector/resources_to_open_in_new_inspector or if this setting is false, attempting to edit a subresource always opens a new inspector view.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/open_resources_in_current_inspector
name: interface/inspector/open_resources_in_current_inspector

description:
List of resources that should always be opened in a new inspector view, even if interface/inspector/open_resources_in_current_inspector is true.

Note: The returned array is copied and any changes to it will not update the original property value. See PackedStringArray for more details.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/resources_to_open_in_new_inspector
name: interface/inspector/resources_to_open_in_new_inspector

description: If true, display OpenType features marked as hidden by the font file in the Font editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/inspector/show_low_level_opentype_features
name: interface/inspector/show_low_level_opentype_features

description:
If true, multiple window support in editor is enabled. The following panels can become dedicated windows (i.e. made floating): Docks, Script editor, Shader editor, and Game Workspace.

\ Note: When interface/editor/display/single_window_mode is true, the multi window support is always disabled.

\ Note: To query whether the editor can use multiple windows in an editor plugin, use EditorInterface.is_multi_window_enabled() instead of querying the value of this editor setting.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/multi_window/enable
name: interface/multi_window/enable

description:
If true, when panels are made floating they will be maximized.

If false, when panels are made floating their position and size will match the ones when they are attached (excluding window border) to the editor window.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/multi_window/maximize_window
name: interface/multi_window/maximize_window

description: If true, the floating panel position, size, and screen will be saved on editor exit. On next launch the panels that were floating will be made floating in the saved positions, sizes and screens, if possible.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/multi_window/restore_windows_on_load
name: interface/multi_window/restore_windows_on_load

description: If true, the FileSystem dock will automatically navigate to the currently selected scene tab.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/scene_tabs/auto_select_current_scene_file
name: interface/scene_tabs/auto_select_current_scene_file

description: Controls when the Close (X) button is displayed on scene tabs at the top of the editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/scene_tabs/display_close_button
name: interface/scene_tabs/display_close_button

description: The maximum width of each scene tab at the top editor (in pixels).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/scene_tabs/maximum_width
name: interface/scene_tabs/maximum_width

description:
If true, when a project is loaded, restores scenes that were opened on the last editor session.

\ Note: With many opened scenes, the editor may take longer to become usable. If starting the editor quickly is necessary, consider setting this to false.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/scene_tabs/restore_scenes_on_load
name: interface/scene_tabs/restore_scenes_on_load

description: If true, show a button next to each scene tab that opens the scene's "dominant" script when clicked. The "dominant" script is the one that is at the highest level in the scene's hierarchy.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/scene_tabs/show_script_button
name: interface/scene_tabs/show_script_button

description: If true, display an automatically-generated thumbnail when hovering scene tabs with the mouse. Scene thumbnails are generated when saving the scene.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/scene_tabs/show_thumbnail_on_hover
name: interface/scene_tabs/show_thumbnail_on_hover

description: The color to use for "highlighted" user interface elements in the editor (pressed and hovered items).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/accent_color
name: interface/theme/accent_color

description:
The extra spacing to add to various GUI elements in the editor (in pixels). Increasing this value is useful to improve usability on touch screens, at the cost of reducing the amount of usable screen real estate.

See also interface/theme/spacing_preset.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/additional_spacing
name: interface/theme/additional_spacing

description: The base color to use for user interface elements in the editor. Secondary colors (such as darker/lighter variants) are derived from this color.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/base_color
name: interface/theme/base_color

description: The base spacing used by various GUI elements in the editor (in pixels). See also interface/theme/spacing_preset.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/base_spacing
name: interface/theme/base_spacing

description: The border size to use for interface elements (in pixels).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/border_size
name: interface/theme/border_size

description: The editor color preset to use.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/color_preset
name: interface/theme/color_preset

description: The contrast factor to use when deriving the editor theme's base color (see interface/theme/base_color). When using positive values, the derived colors will be darker than the base color. This contrast factor can be set to a negative value, which will make the derived colors brighter than the base color. Negative contrast rates often look better for light themes.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/contrast
name: interface/theme/contrast

description: The corner radius to use for interface elements (in pixels). 0 is square.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/corner_radius
name: interface/theme/corner_radius

description: The custom theme resource to use for the editor. Must be a Godot theme resource in .tres or .res format.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/custom_theme
name: interface/theme/custom_theme

description: If true, draws additional borders around interactive UI elements in the editor. This is automatically enabled when using the Black (OLED) theme preset, as this theme preset uses a fully black background.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/draw_extra_borders
name: interface/theme/draw_extra_borders

description:
What relationship lines to draw in the editor's Tree-based GUIs (such as the Scene tree dock).

- None will make it so that no relationship lines are drawn.

- Selected Only will only draw them for selected items.

- All will always draw them for all items.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/draw_relationship_lines
name: interface/theme/draw_relationship_lines

description: If true, the editor theme preset will attempt to automatically match the system theme.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/follow_system_theme
name: interface/theme/follow_system_theme

description:
The icon and font color scheme to use in the editor.

- Auto determines the color scheme to use automatically based on interface/theme/base_color.

- Dark makes fonts and icons dark (suitable for light themes). Icon colors are automatically converted by the editor following the set of rules defined in this file <https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/editor/themes/editor_theme_manager.cpp>_.

- Light makes fonts and icons light (suitable for dark themes).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/icon_and_font_color
name: interface/theme/icon_and_font_color

description:
The saturation to use for editor icons. Higher values result in more vibrant colors.

\ Note: The default editor icon saturation was increased by 30% in Godot 4.0 and later. To get Godot 3.x's icon saturation back, set interface/theme/icon_saturation to 0.77.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/icon_saturation
name: interface/theme/icon_saturation

description: The opacity to use when drawing relationship lines in the editor's Tree-based GUIs (such as the Scene tree dock).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/relationship_line_opacity
name: interface/theme/relationship_line_opacity

description: The editor theme spacing preset to use. See also interface/theme/base_spacing and interface/theme/additional_spacing.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/spacing_preset
name: interface/theme/spacing_preset

description: The editor theme style to use.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/style
name: interface/theme/style

description: If true, use the monospace font for some labels in the editor that display code symbols, such as signals, properties, and methods.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/use_monospace_font_for_editor_symbols
name: interface/theme/use_monospace_font_for_editor_symbols

description:
If true, set accent color based on system settings.

\ Note: This setting is effective on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/theme/use_system_accent_color
name: interface/theme/use_system_accent_color

description:
If true, long press on touchscreen is treated as right click.

\ Note: Defaults to true on touchscreen devices.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/touchscreen/enable_long_press_as_right_click
name: interface/touchscreen/enable_long_press_as_right_click

description:
If true, enable two finger pan and scale gestures on touchscreen devices.

\ Note: Defaults to true on touchscreen devices.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/touchscreen/enable_pan_and_scale_gestures
name: interface/touchscreen/enable_pan_and_scale_gestures

description:
If true, increases the scrollbar touch area, enables a larger dragger for split containers, and increases PopupMenu vertical separation to improve usability on touchscreen devices.

\ Note: Defaults to true on touchscreen devices.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/touchscreen/enable_touch_optimizations
name: interface/touchscreen/enable_touch_optimizations

description:
If true, the device will vibrate when a long-press gesture triggers a right-click context menu in the editor.

\ Note: Only has an effect on devices with haptic feedback hardware. Defaults to true on touchscreen devices.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/touchscreen/haptic_on_long_press
name: interface/touchscreen/haptic_on_long_press

description:
Specify the multiplier to apply to the scale for the editor gizmo handles to improve usability on touchscreen devices.

\ Note: Defaults to 1 on non-touchscreen devices.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/touchscreen/scale_gizmo_handles
name: interface/touchscreen/scale_gizmo_handles

description:
A touch-friendly panel that provides easy access to common actions such as save, delete, undo, and redo without requiring a keyboard.

\ Note: Only available in the Android and XR editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_interface/touchscreen/touch_actions_panel
name: interface/touchscreen/touch_actions_panel

description:
Specifies how the engine should check for updates.

- Disable Update Checks will block the engine from checking updates (see also network/connection/network_mode).

- Auto (default) will check for newest stable or unstable version, depending on which version are you currently using. Switch to another option if you want to lock in.

- Check Newest Preview will check for the newest available development snapshot.

- Check Newest Stable will check for the newest available stable version.

- Check Newest Patch will check for the latest available stable version, but only within the same minor version. E.g. if your version is 4.3.stable, you will be notified about 4.3.1.stable, but not 4.4.stable.

All update modes will ignore builds with different major versions (e.g. Godot 4 -> Godot 5).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/connection/check_for_updates
name: network/connection/check_for_updates

description:
Determines whether online features, such as the Asset Store or update checks, are enabled in the editor. If this is a privacy concern, disabling these online features prevents the editor from making HTTP requests to the Godot website or third-party platforms hosting assets from the Asset Store.

Editor plugins and tool scripts are recommended to follow this setting. However, Godot can't prevent them from violating this rule.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/connection/network_mode
name: network/connection/network_mode

description: The address to listen to when starting the remote debugger. This can be set to this device's local IP address to allow external clients to connect to the remote debugger (instead of restricting the remote debugger to connections from localhost).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/debug/remote_host
name: network/debug/remote_host

description: The port to listen to when starting the remote debugger. Godot will try to use port numbers above the configured number if the configured number is already taken by another application.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/debug/remote_port
name: network/debug/remote_port

description:
The host to use to contact the HTTP and HTTPS proxy in the editor (for the asset store and export template downloads). See also network/http_proxy/port.

\ Note: Godot currently doesn't automatically use system proxy settings, so you have to enter them manually here if needed.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/http_proxy/host
name: network/http_proxy/host

description:
The port number to use to contact the HTTP and HTTPS proxy in the editor (for the asset store and export template downloads). See also network/http_proxy/host.

\ Note: Godot currently doesn't automatically use system proxy settings, so you have to enter them manually here if needed.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/http_proxy/port
name: network/http_proxy/port

description:
If true the language server will try to provide additional results when resolving symbols at the cost of showing wrong results. All symbols in the project are checked and resolved just based on their name, without taking context into account.

::

func untyped(param):
param.print() # Will resolve to the global print method for e.g. hover hints.

When using static typing it is recommended to disable this setting, since it will mostly add false positives for typed code.

\ Note: This setting also influences how symbols are resolved when using renaming capabilities.

\ Note: The default value of this setting might change in future versions.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/language_server/enable_smart_resolve
name: network/language_server/enable_smart_resolve

description: The upper limit of time, that the language server spends for IO each poll.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/language_server/poll_limit_usec
name: network/language_server/poll_limit_usec

description: The host used to listen for language server clients.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/language_server/remote_host
name: network/language_server/remote_host

description:
The port used to listen for language server clients.

\ Note: A port configured with command-line options will take priority over this setting: --lsp-port <port>.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/language_server/remote_port
name: network/language_server/remote_port

description:
The declaration of native symbols can't be resolved to a position in the file system. If true the language server will instead open the documentation for native symbols in the editor.

\ Note: The VSCode plugin adds additional functionality which allows viewing Godot documentation directly in VSCode, so this option is usually not needed in VSCode.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/language_server/show_native_symbols_in_editor
name: network/language_server/show_native_symbols_in_editor

description: If true the language server will run in a separate thread, if false it will run on the main thread.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/language_server/use_thread
name: network/language_server/use_thread

description: The TLS certificate bundle to use for HTTP requests made within the editor (e.g. from the Asset Store tab). If left empty, the included Mozilla certificate bundle <https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/thirdparty/certs/ca-bundle.crt>_ will be used.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/tls/editor_tls_certificates
name: network/tls/editor_tls_certificates

description:
If true, enable TLSv1.3 negotiation.

\ Note: Only supported when using Mbed TLS 3.0 or later (Linux distribution packages may be compiled against older system Mbed TLS packages), otherwise the maximum supported TLS version is always TLSv1.2.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_network/tls/enable_tls_v1.3
name: network/tls/enable_tls_v1.3

description: The renderer type that will be checked off by default when creating a new project. Accepted strings are "forward_plus", "mobile" or "gl_compatibility".
label: class_EditorSettings_property_project_manager/default_renderer
name: project_manager/default_renderer

description: Directory naming convention for the project manager. Options are "No Convention" (project name is directory name), "kebab-case" (default), "snake_case", "camelCase", "PascalCase", or "Title Case".
label: class_EditorSettings_property_project_manager/directory_naming_convention
name: project_manager/directory_naming_convention

description: The sorting order to use in the project manager. When changing the sorting order in the project manager, this setting is set permanently in the editor settings.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_project_manager/sorting_order
name: project_manager/sorting_order

description: If true, saves all scenes and scripts automatically before running the project. Setting this to false prevents the editor from saving if there are no changes which can speed up the project startup slightly, but it makes it possible to run a project that has unsaved changes. (Unsaved changes will not be visible in the running project.)
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/auto_save/save_before_running
name: run/auto_save/save_before_running

description:
The action to execute on the bottom panel when running the project.

\ Note: This option won't do anything if the bottom panel switching is locked using the pin button in the corner of the bottom panel.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/bottom_panel/action_on_play
name: run/bottom_panel/action_on_play

description:
The action to execute on the bottom panel when stopping the project.

\ Note: This option won't do anything if the bottom panel switching is locked using the pin button in the corner of the bottom panel.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/bottom_panel/action_on_stop
name: run/bottom_panel/action_on_stop

description: If true, the editor will clear the Output panel when running the project.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/output/always_clear_output_on_play
name: run/output/always_clear_output_on_play

description: The size of the font in the Output panel at the bottom of the editor. This setting does not impact the font size of the script editor (see interface/editor/fonts/code_font_size).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/output/font_size
name: run/output/font_size

description: Maximum number of lines to show at any one time in the Output panel.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/output/max_lines
name: run/output/max_lines

description: If true, on Linux/BSD, the editor will check for Wayland first instead of X11 (if available).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/platforms/linuxbsd/prefer_wayland
name: run/platforms/linuxbsd/prefer_wayland

description:
Specifies how the Play window is launched relative to the Android editor.

- Auto (based on screen size) (default) will automatically choose how to launch the Play window based on the device and screen metrics. Defaults to Same as Editor on phones and Side-by-side with Editor on tablets.

- Same as Editor will launch the Play window in the same window as the Editor.

- Side-by-side with Editor will launch the Play window side-by-side with the Editor window.

\ Note: Only available in the Android editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/window_placement/android_window
name: run/window_placement/android_window

description: Overrides game embedding setting for all newly opened projects. If enabled, game embedding settings are not saved.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/window_placement/game_embed_mode
name: run/window_placement/game_embed_mode

description:
The window mode to use to display the project when starting the project from the editor.

\ Note: Game embedding is not available for "Force Maximized" or "Force Fullscreen".
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/window_placement/rect
name: run/window_placement/rect

description: The custom position to use when starting the project from the editor (in pixels from the top-left corner). Only effective if run/window_placement/rect is set to Custom Position.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/window_placement/rect_custom_position
name: run/window_placement/rect_custom_position

description: The monitor to display the project on when starting the project from the editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_run/window_placement/screen
name: run/window_placement/screen

description: If true, makes the caret blink according to text_editor/appearance/caret/caret_blink_interval. Disabling this setting can improve battery life on laptops if you spend long amounts of time in the script editor, since it will reduce the frequency at which the editor needs to be redrawn.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/caret/caret_blink
name: text_editor/appearance/caret/caret_blink

description: The interval at which the caret will blink (in seconds). See also text_editor/appearance/caret/caret_blink.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/caret/caret_blink_interval
name: text_editor/appearance/caret/caret_blink_interval

description: If true, highlights all occurrences of the currently selected text in the script editor. See also text_editor/theme/highlighting/word_highlighted_color.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/caret/highlight_all_occurrences
name: text_editor/appearance/caret/highlight_all_occurrences

description: If true, colors the background of the line the caret is currently on with text_editor/theme/highlighting/current_line_color.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/caret/highlight_current_line
name: text_editor/appearance/caret/highlight_current_line

description: The shape of the caret to use in the script editor. Line displays a vertical line to the left of the current character, whereas Block displays an outline over the current character.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/caret/type
name: text_editor/appearance/caret/type

description: If true, shows an info label listing available drop options when dragging an object into the script text editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/drag_and_drop_info/show_drag_and_drop_info
name: text_editor/appearance/drag_and_drop_info/show_drag_and_drop_info

description: If true, displays a colored button before any Color constructor in the script editor. Clicking on them allows the color to be modified through a color picker.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/enable_inline_color_picker
name: text_editor/appearance/enable_inline_color_picker

description: The column at which to display a subtle line as a line length guideline for scripts. This should generally be greater than text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_soft_column.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_hard_column
name: text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_hard_column

description: The column at which to display a very subtle line as a line length guideline for scripts. This should generally be lower than text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_hard_column.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_soft_column
name: text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_soft_column

description: If true, displays line length guidelines to help you keep line lengths in check. See also text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_soft_column and text_editor/appearance/guidelines/line_length_guideline_hard_column.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/guidelines/show_line_length_guidelines
name: text_editor/appearance/guidelines/show_line_length_guidelines

description: If true, highlights type-safe lines by displaying their line number color with text_editor/theme/highlighting/safe_line_number_color instead of text_editor/theme/highlighting/line_number_color. Type-safe lines are lines of code where the type of all variables is known at compile-time. These type-safe lines may run faster thanks to typed instructions.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/gutters/highlight_type_safe_lines
name: text_editor/appearance/gutters/highlight_type_safe_lines

description: If true, displays line numbers with zero padding (e.g. 007 instead of 7).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/gutters/line_numbers_zero_padded
name: text_editor/appearance/gutters/line_numbers_zero_padded

description: If true, displays a gutter at the left containing icons for methods with signal connections and for overridden methods.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/gutters/show_info_gutter
name: text_editor/appearance/gutters/show_info_gutter

description: If true, displays line numbers in a gutter at the left.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/gutters/show_line_numbers
name: text_editor/appearance/gutters/show_line_numbers

description: If text_editor/appearance/lines/word_wrap is set to 1, sets text wrapping mode. To see how each mode behaves, see AutowrapMode.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/lines/autowrap_mode
name: text_editor/appearance/lines/autowrap_mode

description: If true, displays the folding arrows next to indented code sections and allows code folding. If false, hides the folding arrows next to indented code sections and disallows code folding.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/lines/code_folding
name: text_editor/appearance/lines/code_folding

description: If true, wraps long lines over multiple lines to avoid horizontal scrolling. This is a display-only feature; it does not actually insert line breaks in your scripts.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/lines/word_wrap
name: text_editor/appearance/lines/word_wrap

description: The width of the minimap in the script editor (in pixels).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/minimap/minimap_width
name: text_editor/appearance/minimap/minimap_width

description: If true, draws an overview of the script near the scroll bar. The minimap can be left-clicked to scroll directly to a location in an "absolute" manner.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/minimap/show_minimap
name: text_editor/appearance/minimap/show_minimap

description: If true, draws space characters as centered points.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/whitespace/draw_spaces
name: text_editor/appearance/whitespace/draw_spaces

description: If true, draws tab characters as chevrons.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/whitespace/draw_tabs
name: text_editor/appearance/whitespace/draw_tabs

description: The space to add between lines (in pixels). Greater line spacing can help improve readability at the cost of displaying fewer lines on screen. Negative values allow for even more compact text, but may look broken with certain fonts.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/appearance/whitespace/line_spacing
name: text_editor/appearance/whitespace/line_spacing

description: If true, documentation tooltips will appear when hovering over a symbol.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/documentation/enable_tooltips
name: text_editor/behavior/documentation/enable_tooltips

description: If true, tool scripts will be automatically soft-reloaded after they are saved.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/auto_reload_and_parse_scripts_on_save
name: text_editor/behavior/files/auto_reload_and_parse_scripts_on_save

description:
If true, automatically reloads scripts and text-based shaders in the editor when they have been modified and saved by external editors or tools and the editor regains focus. External changes can be discarded by using the Undo function after they've been loaded in the editor.

If false, a file conflict dialog will always be displayed when the editor regains focus. This dialog allows you to choose whether to keep local changes or discard them.

\ Note: Even when this setting is true, a file conflict dialog is still displayed in certain situations. For instance, it will display when the script editor has unsaved changes that the external editor did not account for.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/auto_reload_scripts_on_external_change
name: text_editor/behavior/files/auto_reload_scripts_on_external_change

description: If set to a value greater than 0, automatically saves the current script following the specified interval (in seconds). This can be used to prevent data loss if the editor crashes.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/autosave_interval_secs
name: text_editor/behavior/files/autosave_interval_secs

description: If true, converts indentation to match the script editor's indentation settings when saving a script. See also text_editor/behavior/indent/type.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/convert_indent_on_save
name: text_editor/behavior/files/convert_indent_on_save

description:
If true, when dropping a Resource file to script editor while Ctrl is held, the resource will be preloaded with a UID. If false, the resource will be preloaded with a path.

When you hold Ctrl+Shift, the behavior is reversed.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/drop_preload_resources_as_uid
name: text_editor/behavior/files/drop_preload_resources_as_uid

description: If true, opening a scene automatically opens the script attached to the root node, or the topmost node if the root has no script.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/open_dominant_script_on_scene_change
name: text_editor/behavior/files/open_dominant_script_on_scene_change

description: If true, reopens scripts that were opened in the last session when the editor is reopened on a given project.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/restore_scripts_on_load
name: text_editor/behavior/files/restore_scripts_on_load

description: If true, trims all empty newlines after the final newline when saving a script. Final newlines refer to the empty newlines found at the end of files. Since these serve no practical purpose, they can and should be removed to make version control diffs less noisy.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/trim_final_newlines_on_save
name: text_editor/behavior/files/trim_final_newlines_on_save

description: If true, trims trailing whitespace when saving a script. Trailing whitespace refers to tab and space characters placed at the end of lines. Since these serve no practical purpose, they can and should be removed to make version control diffs less noisy.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/files/trim_trailing_whitespace_on_save
name: text_editor/behavior/files/trim_trailing_whitespace_on_save

description: If true, copying or cutting without a selection is performed on all lines with a caret. Otherwise, copy and cut require a selection.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/general/empty_selection_clipboard
name: text_editor/behavior/general/empty_selection_clipboard

description: If true, automatically indents code when pressing the Enter key based on blocks above the new line.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/indent/auto_indent
name: text_editor/behavior/indent/auto_indent

description: If true, all wrapped lines are indented to the same amount as the unwrapped line.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/indent/indent_wrapped_lines
name: text_editor/behavior/indent/indent_wrapped_lines

description: When using tab indentation, determines the length of each tab. When using space indentation, determines how many spaces are inserted when pressing Tab and when automatic indentation is performed.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/indent/size
name: text_editor/behavior/indent/size

description:
The indentation style to use (tabs or spaces).

\ Note: The GDScript style guide recommends using tabs for indentation. It is advised to change this setting only if you need to work on a project that currently uses spaces for indentation.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/indent/type
name: text_editor/behavior/indent/type

description: The characters to consider as word delimiters if text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_custom_word_separators is true. This is in addition to default characters if text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_default_word_separators is true. The characters should be defined without separation, for example _♥=.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/custom_word_separators
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/custom_word_separators

description: If true, allows drag-and-dropping text in the script editor to move text. Disable this if you find yourself accidentally drag-and-dropping text in the script editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/drag_and_drop_selection
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/drag_and_drop_selection

description: If true, the caret will be moved when right-clicking somewhere in the script editor (like when left-clicking or middle-clicking). If false, the caret will only be moved when left-clicking or middle-clicking somewhere.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/move_caret_on_right_click
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/move_caret_on_right_click

description: If true, opens the script editor when connecting a signal to an existing script method from the Signals dock.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/open_script_when_connecting_signal_to_existing_method
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/open_script_when_connecting_signal_to_existing_method

description: If true, allows scrolling past the end of the file.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/scroll_past_end_of_file
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/scroll_past_end_of_file

description:
If true, enables a smooth scrolling animation when using the mouse wheel to scroll. See text_editor/behavior/navigation/v_scroll_speed for the speed of this animation.

\ Note: text_editor/behavior/navigation/smooth_scrolling currently behaves poorly in projects where ProjectSettings.physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second has been increased significantly from its default value (60). In this case, it is recommended to disable this setting.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/smooth_scrolling
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/smooth_scrolling

description: If true, prevents automatically switching between the Script and 2D/3D screens when selecting a node in the Scene tree dock.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/stay_in_script_editor_on_node_selected
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/stay_in_script_editor_on_node_selected

description: If true, uses the characters in text_editor/behavior/navigation/custom_word_separators as word separators for word navigation and operations. This is in addition to the default characters if text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_default_word_separators is also enabled. Word navigation and operations include double-clicking on a word or holding Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) while pressing left, right, backspace, or delete.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_custom_word_separators
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_custom_word_separators

description: If true, uses the characters in ```!"#$%&'()+,-./:;<=>?@[]^`{}~, the Unicode General Punctuation table, and the Unicode CJK Punctuation table as word separators for word navigation and operations. If false, a subset of these characters are used and does not include the characters <>$~^=+``. This is in addition to custom characters if text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_custom_word_separators is also enabled. These characters are used to determine where a word stops. Word navigation and operations include double-clicking on a word or holding Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) while pressing left, right, backspace, or delete.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_default_word_separators
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/use_default_word_separators

description:
The speed of scrolling in lines per second when text_editor/behavior/navigation/smooth_scrolling is true. Higher values make the script scroll by faster when using the mouse wheel.

\ Note: You can hold down Alt while using the mouse wheel to temporarily scroll 5 times faster.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/behavior/navigation/v_scroll_speed
name: text_editor/behavior/navigation/v_scroll_speed

description: If true, uses NodePath instead of String when appropriate for code autocompletion or for drag and dropping object properties into the script editor.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/add_node_path_literals
name: text_editor/completion/add_node_path_literals

description: If true, uses StringName instead of String when appropriate for code autocompletion.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/add_string_name_literals
name: text_editor/completion/add_string_name_literals

label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/add_type_hints
name: text_editor/completion/add_type_hints

description: If true, automatically inserts the matching closing brace when the opening brace is inserted by typing or autocompletion. Also automatically removes the closing brace when pressing Backspace on the opening brace. This includes brackets ((), [], {}), string quotation marks ('', ""), and comments (//) if the language supports it.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/auto_brace_complete
name: text_editor/completion/auto_brace_complete

description: The delay in seconds after which autocompletion suggestions should be displayed when the user stops typing.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/code_complete_delay
name: text_editor/completion/code_complete_delay

description: If true, code completion will be triggered automatically after text_editor/completion/code_complete_delay. Even if false, code completion can be triggered manually with the ui_text_completion_query action (by default Ctrl + Space or Cmd + Space on macOS).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/code_complete_enabled
name: text_editor/completion/code_complete_enabled

description: If true enables the coloring for some items in the autocompletion suggestions, like vector components.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/colorize_suggestions
name: text_editor/completion/colorize_suggestions

description: If true, provides autocompletion suggestions for file paths in methods such as load() and preload().
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/complete_file_paths
name: text_editor/completion/complete_file_paths

description: The delay in seconds after which the script editor should check for errors when the user stops typing.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/idle_parse_delay
name: text_editor/completion/idle_parse_delay

description: The delay used instead of text_editor/completion/idle_parse_delay, when the parser has found errors. A lower value should feel more responsive while fixing code, but may cause notable stuttering and increase CPU usage.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/idle_parse_delay_with_errors_found
name: text_editor/completion/idle_parse_delay_with_errors_found

description: If true, the code completion tooltip will appear below the current line unless there is no space on screen below the current line. If false, the code completion tooltip will appear above the current line.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/put_callhint_tooltip_below_current_line
name: text_editor/completion/put_callhint_tooltip_below_current_line

description: If true, performs string autocompletion with single quotes. If false, performs string autocompletion with double quotes (which matches the GDScript style guide).
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/completion/use_single_quotes
name: text_editor/completion/use_single_quotes

description: The command-line arguments to pass to the external text editor that is run when text_editor/external/use_external_editor is true. See also text_editor/external/exec_path.
label: class_EditorSettings_property_text_editor/external/exec_flags
name: text_editor/external/exec_flags
